A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StochNASim/PPO study. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-B are readable and matchable despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5.2-5.4 report original simulation results comparing PPO variants and fixed versus stochastic network training. Appendix A includes empirical hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains the original learning curves, network-size comparisons, policy analyses, generalization experiments and appendix sensitivity results.

M1.justification: StochNASim generation and action padding, the element-wise maximum observation-aggregation wrapper, frame stacking, LSTM and Transformer-XL procedures remain unchanged. Expanded observation descriptions disclose existing behavior rather than establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate penetration testing on synthetic networks with 5-8 hosts, including fixed NASim scenarios and newly generated StochNASim configurations. Networks exceeding 20 hosts are mentioned only as future work in v2.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same PPO, PPO-FS, PPO-AO, PPO-LSTM and PPO-TrXL comparators and the NASim/StochNASim comparison. DQN and SAC are proposed for future investigation, not evaluated.

E3.justification: Environment parameters, hyperparameter search ranges and selections, training budgets, evaluation intervals and policy-analysis procedures match across versions. The 100 novel networks specified in v2 Section 5.4 newly document the existing evaluation's sample size without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: Network-size sensitivity, action distributions, representative action sequences, stochasticity/generalization comparisons and appendix fANOVA analysis are retained. v2's additional discussion of Figure 8 does not introduce another analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed aggregation, the same explicit seed list, IQM/rliable reporting and shaded variability bands. v2 adds numerical ±5 summaries for existing results, but no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence level or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: The headline convergence estimate changes from threefold to up to fourfold. v2 newly states NASim training reward of 195±5, StochNASim training/test reward of 167±5, and less than 15% architectural-parameter importance. These refine numerical reporting; the plotted results and rankings in Figures 3-8 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP/POMDP definitions, reward equation and observation-aggregation mathematics are retained. Explicitly listing the scan-action set and correcting a closing parenthesis do not change the mathematical substance. Neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace the threefold convergence claim with up to fourfold, consistent with the existing Section 5.2 comparison. v2 more explicitly confines the evaluation to PPO-based methods and the conclusion to on-policy simulation evidence; the principal contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds an algorithm-task-fit interpretation of the existing fANOVA results and elaborates observation-sequence memorization under fixed-scenario training. It also explicitly leaves generalization to larger networks and off-policy algorithms unresolved. The previously stated limitation concerning dynamic host states remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a StochNASim repository address and states that StochNASim/PPO-TrXL code accompanies the supplementary material. It explains zero-valued observation encoding and specifies 100 novel evaluation networks, while shortening some host-encoding details. Hyperparameters, hardware, software version and seed disclosures otherwise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dai et al. on Transformer-XL and Lyon's Nmap reference. Related work additionally questions whether insufficient hyperparameter tuning explains earlier reported gains. These are limited additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 moves and condenses penetration-testing background before the formal RL material, rewrites selected related-work and environment passages, numbers methodological subsections and moves tuning-library details into Appendix A. Terminology and citation style are updated, while most prose and the overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different page geometry, typography, headers and figure placement throughout. A new NASim/StochNASim comparison table is added, Figure 3 changes from a two-row arrangement to one row, and several retained figures are substantially resized. The eight figures' underlying image content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and reproducibility through explicit observation semantics, code-access information and clearer limits concerning PPO and network scale. It also aligns the headline speedup with Section 5.2. These are useful reporting improvements to unchanged empirical evidence, although the new ±5 reward summaries still lack a defined uncertainty statistic.
